ECE 6390

DVB-S2: from payload to waveform

From the figure to the concept

Fig. 1 shows how a useful bit stream passes through the protection and waveform stages of a satellite broadcast.

DVB-S2 supplies selectable satellite modulation-and-coding profiles. In the transmit chain, an outer BCH block code adds protection, an inner LDPC code adds further constraints, a mapper assigns coded bits to symbols, and physical framing supplies synchronization and optional pilots. A receiver reverses these roles after synchronizing. Bit interleaving is used for 8PSK and APSK; the QPSK path bypasses that interleaver.

For full occupied raised-cosine RF width B and rolloff α, Rs = B/(1+α). The mapper handles Rcoded = Rs log₂M. Useful information is reduced by coding and framing: Rinfo = η r Rs log₂M when r represents every code stage being counted and η represents the remaining resource fraction. An inner-LDPC rate alone is not the complete payload fraction.

The adjustable figure uses a small set of allowed DVB-S2 normal-frame profiles. A normal FEC frame contains 64800 LDPC-coded bits. It accounts for the chosen BCH information size, the 80-bit baseband header, the 90-symbol physical header and optional 36-symbol pilot blocks after groups of 16 slots. The example assumes a completely filled baseband frame and no input-packet or padding loss.

Rate choices and constellation choices are separate controls but only supported pairs form actual standard profiles. The lecture’s inner-LDPC rates span 1/4 through 9/10. At the QPSK end, lowering rate can provide more protection while reducing useful throughput. These controls account for resource usage. Link feasibility also needs a profile’s required received quality and a selected error target.

Example

For a 6 MHz channel before coding/framing, QPSK withα =0.35 maps 8.89 Mbit/s; 32APSK withα =0.20 maps 25 Mbit/s. Their ratio is 2.8125. Both values count coded labels, so a payload-rate comparison must also include each profile’s code and overhead.

Practice

1. Why does selecting a listed inner rate 3/4 fail to establish that 75% of every RF symbol is useful payload?

Follow both coding stages and the framing resources.

BCH parity, the baseband header, the physical header and any pilots also use resources. The useful fraction needs the complete chain, not only the inner-LDPC ratio.

2. If a fade already forced QPSK, how can the system trade still more throughput for protection?

A MODCOD contains a coding choice as well as a constellation.

It can choose a supported lower coding rate. More of the transmitted stream then carries redundancy, reducing useful information rate while potentially improving reliability for the stated decoder.
